cells.tense: Right now you are seeing clearly, and the person across from you can feel it.
cells.ask: Tell one person the thing you noticed about them before you decide if it's useful. Say it plain, then leave it with them.
cells.core:
You meet people through what you see fresh, and it's happening right now. Whatever is in front of you arrives clear before you've had time to label it, and you don't rush the label. So people feel seen by you, not studied.

It could go further than it has. Stay with the pattern under one hard thing and you go deeper without going distant. Keeping it costs something: the moment you start managing what you catch, you're at the desk again, not in the room. So stay open to what shows up, even the unflattering bits, and keep the contact alive rather than the conclusion tidy. The person gets you as someone who looks, not someone who already looked.
cells.sheetLine: You see people clearly, and it lands as contact.

cells.tense: You are reading how this will go from the far side, and you haven't gotten there yet.
cells.ask: Go into one conversation with nothing prepared. Let yourself not know, ask what's actually happening, and stay till they finish.
cells.core:
You read people ahead of the moment they're in. Up ahead there's a scene where it all fits, and you already live there — deciding what they'll say, what it'll mean, what you'll answer. The read is sharp. The timing is off.

When you're braced like that, the person across from you gets your forecast instead of you. They can feel it, even when you're right. Coming back looks like setting the read down and showing up open — no angle, nothing to guard. What you notice is worth having; it just can't be handed over from tomorrow. Being here while you notice is the whole of it.

cells.tense: You set it down a while back, and the room you walked out of is still behind you.
cells.ask: Say one true thing you see about someone you live or work with, out loud. Small is fine. Then stay for the next sentence.
cells.core:
Contact with people is running thin, and your eye goes with it. You've been careful in rooms, tuned to the surface, present but not with anyone. You pulled the lens in and left it there.

This doesn't need feeling pushed back in. It needs something pointed: one clear thing you choose to say, one small step toward someone, however it lands. A day of that and your eye returns on its own. You won't have to force yourself to care — the caring didn't go anywhere. It just stopped being aimed at anyone. Aim it at something. The old room can stay where it is.

cells.tense: You already catch what people walk past, and you call it just being observant.
cells.ask: Name one thing you noticed about someone today and say it to them without explaining. Short. No setup, no theory.
cells.core:
You already catch what most people miss — the shift in someone's voice, the thing under the thing they said — and you don't call it anything. You file it and move on. That eye is yours, arriving fresh, and it shapes how you're with people whether you claim it or not.

Claiming it isn't a big move. It's admitting, once, that you're the one doing it, not just a good listener who happens to catch things. That's the entry point. Not a system, not a payoff — a moment where you're here and catch something, and you could just as easily be elsewhere. Say what you saw, and let it be something you did rather than something that landed on you.
